en.title: Stress and Vowel Contrast
en.summary: Learn how word stress changes vowel strength and quality at the ends of Romanian words.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Listen to the word endings carefully. A stressed ending sounds strong, clear, and long. An unstressed ending sounds light, quick, and soft. Listen to (vorbesc) /vorˈbesk/, which means I speak. The stress is on the last part. The vowel sounds clear. In (vorbește) /vorˈbeʃ.te/, meaning he speaks, the last vowel is soft and quick.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Open your mouth wider for a stressed ending. Push more air from your lungs. Make your voice higher and hold the vowel longer. For an unstressed ending, drop your jaw less. Use less air and keep your voice relaxed. Say (vorbesc) /vorˈbesk/. Hit the ending like the word 'desk'. Keep the sound punchy and bright.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Romanian does not use written accent marks to show stress. You must learn which part gets the push. Verbs often put strong stress right on the final ending. Look at (vorbesc) /vorˈbesk/. The final letter e receives full power. Never hide or swallow a stressed ending vowel. Read it out loud with full energy.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make every vowel equal in strength. Some learners say words flatly. In (vorbesc) /vorˈbesk/, do not stress the first part. Push only on the ending. Also, do not change stressed vowels into weak murmurs. Give the stressed vowel its pure sound. Keep unstressed endings softer, but keep stressed endings strong and crisp.
